subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Water Chemistry
description: A quick win: understand Water Chemistry.

hook.text: Coffee is 98% water. If your water tastes bad, your coffee will taste bad—no matter how good the beans are.

buildup.text: Mineral content matters. Calcium and magnesium help extract flavor compounds from coffee grounds.

discovery.text: The Specialty Coffee Association recommends 75–250 ppm total dissolved solids for optimal brewing.

twist.text: Distilled water tastes flat because it lacks minerals to bind with coffee's flavor molecules.

climax.text: Competition baristas custom-build water with precise mineral recipes to maximize extraction quality.

punchline.text: Perfect beans, wrong water, ruined cup. Water is the recipe.

quiz.question: Why does distilled water make poor coffee?
options: It lacks minerals needed to extract flavor compounds

details.summary: Water makes up over 98 percent of brewed coffee, and its mineral content profoundly affects flavor. Calcium and magnesium help extract flavor compounds, while bicarbonates buffer acidity. Water that is too soft produces flat coffee; water that is too hard creates chalky bitterness.
details.whyItMatters: Bad water ruins good coffee. Understanding water chemistry explains why the same beans taste different in different cities.
takeaways: Water is over 98 percent of brewed coffee by volume
Calcium and magnesium enhance flavor extraction
The SCA recommends 75 to 250 ppm total dissolved solids

faq.question: What minerals matter most for coffee brewing?
faq.answer: Magnesium extracts fruity and complex flavors most effectively. Calcium contributes body and heavier mouthfeel. Bicarbonates buffer acids and prevent sourness. The balance between these minerals determines whether water helps or hinders extraction.

faq.question: Should you use filtered or bottled water for coffee?
faq.answer: Filtered water that removes chlorine but retains some minerals is ideal. Distilled or reverse-osmosis water is too empty and produces flat coffee. Some enthusiasts add precise mineral packets to distilled water for complete control.
